question: Do published models identify affinity ordering, and could matching training examples explain correct-looking score changes?
scope: Observed raw binding classifier scores, not measured affinities or evidence for the causal origin of predictions. No retraining or new inference performed in this audit.

membership_findings.ImRex: Both released actual training tables contain native MEL5 CDR3beta+ELA positive. Mature CDR3beta absent including common anchor-normalized forms. G4A and I7A peptides absent for every receptor. Nearest mature CDR3beta training sequence is native MEL5: 15 residues, edit distance4, 11 identical positions. No family exclusion.
membership_findings.NetTCR2.2: Final models trained on limited34352 rows; full37721 rows used for evaluation. Native MEL5+ELA exact six-CDR input occurs in partition0. Mature alpha/beta CDR3 pair+ELA occurs but its A1/A2/B2 fields are native rather than engineered, so not a complete mature six-CDR exact duplicate. All11 known CDR3pair-related rows partition0. G4A/I7A peptides absent across both tables and peptide/original_peptide columns. t0 four models exclude partition0 from training and validation per official nested CV; no checkpoint-specific training-row manifest or full family-exclusion proof.
membership_findings.ERGO-II: G4A/I7A peptides absent from both released checkpoint training pickles. Mature alpha/beta CDR3 absent under checked anchor forms. VDJdb contains native beta+ELA twice, one positive and one negative, both with a different alpha extension. Not two exact full-input positives. VDJdb nearest mature beta is native MEL5 at edit distance4; McPAS nearest distance6.

conclusion: Cannot claim all mainstream predictors recover affinity ordering. No evidence of direct G4A/I7A exact peptide-label memorization in released tables. There is evidence of native/same-family training exposure; correct-looking score changes cannot establish family-independent generalization, and exposure alone does not prove a memorization cause.
